transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Hi, yeah, thank you. So, um, the main reason I finally decided I really needed to make an appointment—which honestly took me forever to actually schedule, I kept opening the clinic website tab and then getting sidetracked by, like, literally anything else—but anyway, the main reason is that I just get pulled off track so incredibly easily. 

It’s like my brain just cannot filter things out. For example, I’ll be sitting down in the library to work on this data dashboard for my seminar class—I'm in my undergrad right now, and it's a pretty big project for my degree—and I'll be trying so hard to just focus and finish it. But then one single Slack ping will go off from my study group. Or, honestly, not even a notification! Sometimes it's literally just a song lyric playing in my headphones, or I'll just get this totally random, out-of-the-blue idea for a completely different project that I'm not even getting graded on. 

And before I even realize it's happening, suddenly I’m twenty tabs deep into researching this new thing, or looking up the meaning of that song lyric, and I’ve completely lost the thread of the dashboard I was actually supposed to be finishing. It's just so frustrating because I know I need to do it, and I know exactly *how* to do it, but it’s like every little thing in the universe is a magnet pulling my attention away, and then I have to spend twenty minutes just trying to remember what I was even looking at before I got derailed. It just happens all the time.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself moving around a lot, even when you're trying to stay focused or sit still?

Oh my gosh, yes. Yes, constantly. It’s actually—well, it’s really uncomfortable, honestly. Like, if I have to sit still, especially if it’s through something like a really long Zoom call for one of my classes, or even just when I’m trying to quietly work in one place at the library like I was mentioning before... I just start feeling this, I don't know, this really intense, uncomfortable pressure in my body. 

It’s almost like my energy gets trapped? And it just builds and builds until I feel like I absolutely *have* to get up and pace around. Like, during my online lectures last semester, I would literally walk laps around my dorm room while listening, just back and forth, because sitting in the desk chair felt physically impossible after maybe fifteen or twenty minutes. I'd even carry my laptop with me so the professor wouldn't see me disappear from the camera frame.

And if I’m in a situation where I really, truly cannot stand up and pace—like if I'm in the middle of an in-person lecture hall or stuck at a quiet study desk—I end up having to do something with my hands just to let that pressure out. I’ll be twisting my rings off and on, or shredding a piece of notebook paper into tiny little confetti pieces, or bouncing my leg so hard the whole table shakes. Which I know totally annoys the people sitting next to me, I've definitely gotten looks from other students before, but if I don't do *something* with my hands or my body, I feel like I'm going to just crawl out of my skin. It's just this constant, buzzing need to be in motion, even when my brain is telling me to just sit down and be normal.
Looking back, did you experience similar issues with restlessness, difficulty staying still, or being easily distracted when you were a child, say before the age of 12?

Oh, wow, yeah. Honestly, it goes way, way back. Like, I remember being in elementary school—second or third grade, I think?—and it was always the same thing. Every single time report cards came out or we had parent-teacher conferences, my teachers would write these super long comments. They were always saying things like, "She rushes through her worksheets," or "She loses track of directions halfway through," and, oh, the big one was always that I talked over my classmates during group work. 

I just couldn't wait my turn, you know? Like, an idea would pop into my head and I felt like I had to blurt it out right that exact second or it would disappear forever, so I was constantly interrupting. And the rushing through things... I just wanted to be done so I could move on to something else, so I'd make all these careless mistakes because I wasn't actually paying attention to what I was doing. 

And homework was a whole other nightmare. My parents literally had to sit right next to me at the kitchen table every single night. Like, they would take turns. My mom would sit with me for math, and my dad would do reading, because if they left me alone for even two minutes to go check on dinner or something, I would completely wander off. They’d come back and find me in the living room playing with my dog, or I’d have pulled out my art supplies and started drawing instead of finishing my spelling sentences. I just could not stick with one task until it was finished unless someone was physically sitting there making sure I didn't drift away. So, yeah, it's definitely been happening for a really, really long time. It's just that now, I don't have my parents sitting next to me to keep me on track, you know? So it feels a lot harder to manage on my own.
